result:
I've fixed F-DG1-232: the shell journey no longer races after the page reload. It passed 120 repeated runs, including a set under CPU load, and the full journeys spec passes in both languages on Node 22 and Node 24. Only the test file changed; no product code.

**Cause:** after `page.reload()`, the test checked only `html[lang]`, which can be correct before the shell has finished mounting. It then pressed Tab at once, and if the shell wasn't there yet the skip link never got focus.

**Fix** (in `apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts`): a new helper, `expectShellReadyForKeyboard()`, runs before the Tab press. It waits until:
- the wordmark, the primary navigation and the main heading are visible;
- My Work is marked as the current page;
- the document has focus and no element is focused yet.

I didn't use the suggested `body.click()`, because a click moves where the next Tab starts from and could land on a link. The skip-link assertion is unchanged. I also added a step: Enter on the skip link must move focus to `<main>`. The code comment already claimed this, but nothing tested it. No other place in `apps/web/e2e` presses a key straight after a reload.

**Checks I ran** (logs in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG1/round-3/T-DG1-FE-R3-evidence/`):

| Run | Node | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Shell journey, 20 repeats per language | 22 | 40/40 passed |
| Same, with every CPU busy plus the web unit tests running alongside | 22 | 40/40 passed |
| Shell journey, 20 repeats per language | 24 | 40/40 passed |
| Full journeys spec, English and Arabic | 22 | 18/18 passed, none skipped |
| Full journeys spec, English and Arabic | 24 | 18/18 passed, none skipped |

`pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `prettier --check` on the edited file and `pnpm test` all exit 0. `pnpm -r typecheck` doesn't cover the `e2e/` folder, so I also type-checked and linted the spec file directly; both passed.

**Things to know:**
- **No screenshots this time.** Nothing visible changed, and I sent this round's screenshots to a temporary directory so the committed ones stay as they were.
- **Not a statistical proof.** Before the fix, the failure showed up about once in 29 runs, or once in 15 under load. 120 clean repeats are strong evidence the race is gone.
- **Node 24 line numbers differ.** On Node 24 the test report shows different line numbers for every test (for example 190 instead of 178 for the shell journey). The file was identical across all runs (same checksum), and the tests, their order and count match, so it's a reporting quirk, not a test difference.
- **QA suite not checked.** I didn't check the QA-owned top-level `e2e/` suite for the same reload-then-key pattern; it's outside my write scope.

I haven't committed anything; the finding stays open until a reviewer other than me verifies the fix. The full handback, with the diff, is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG1/round-3/T-DG1-FE-R3-frontend-ux-engineer.md`.
